question.explanation: 밑줄 (E)에서 ‘regardless of his or her background’는 전통적인 규범 문법에 어긋납니다. 앞에 있는 ‘anyone’을 대명사 ‘his or her’로 받더라도, ‘regardless of’ 뒤에 바로 소유격+명사 구조를 쓰는 것은 부자연스럽습니다. 올바른 표현은 ‘regardless of background’처럼 관사나 소유격 없이 추상적인 명사를 쓰거나, ‘regardless of their background’와 같이 복수 대명사를 사용해 단수 ‘anyone’과 수일치를 현대적 용법으로 해결하는 것입니다.
keyPoints: ‘regardless of’ 뒤에 한정사(his or her)를 붙여 ‘regardless of his or her background’로 쓰는 표현은 전통적인 규범 문법에서 비문으로 간주됩니다.
‘regardless of’는 주로 ‘regardless of + (무관사) 명사’ 형태로 쓰이며, 특정 대명사를 쓸 경우 ‘regardless of their background’와 같이 복수형을 사용할 수 있습니다.

question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment __(A) that is shown in his artwork__. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) where he worked as a freelance artist__. During World War II, he traveled to California, __(C) where he became interested in the media of sculpture__. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, __(D) yet firmly rooted in the special tradition__ of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless of his or her background__.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure __(A) of being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are __(B) suffering from__ reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of __(C) other people__ who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with __(D) you reading friend or partner__ at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody __(E) takes turns__ reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

markedExpressions.label: (E)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'a thousand lines of letters in UNIX'는 하나의 개념으로 다루어지므로 단수 동사 qualifies가 적절하다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'as well'은 '또한'의 의미로 문장 끝에 쓰이는 부사구로, 어법상 아무런 문제가 없다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): something을 수식하는 과거분사로, '만들어진'이라는 수동의 의미를 나타내므로 produced가 올바르다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 'the same category as'에서 as는 전치사로 쓰여 비교 대상을 이끌며, 문법적으로 정확한 용법이다.

question.explanation: 정답은 ⑤ (E) 'technologically'이다. 정답 문장 'Both are technological.'의 골격을 살펴보면, 주어 'Both'는 앞에 언급된 셰익스피어 소네트와 슈베르트 교향곡 같은 문학·예술 작품을 가리키며, 동사 are는 2형식으로 보어를 요구한다. 보어 자리에는 주어의 속성을 서술하는 형용사가 와야 하므로 technological이 적절한 형태다. 그러나 밑줄 친 technologically는 부사로, are를 수식할 요소가 없어 비문을 이루므로 technological로 고쳐야 한다. 한편 (A)의 qualifies는 'a thousand lines of letters'가 하나의 집합체로 인식되어 단수 동사와 결합한 예이며, (D)의 produced는 과거분사로 수동 관계를 나타내므로 어법에 맞다.
keyPoints: (E) 형용사 vs 부사 — be동사 보어 자리에는 형용사가 필요하며, -ly 부사는 틀린 표현이다.
(A) 수의 일치 — a thousand lines of letters가 하나의 덩어리로 간주되어 단수 동사 qualifies를 쓴다.
(D) 분사의 능동·수동 — something과 produce는 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 produced가 올바르다.
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(A) qualifies__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify __(B) as well__. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category __(C) as__ Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(D) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are __(E) technologically__.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but __(B) that can prevent happiness__ in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). __(C) To break out of this neural rut__, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point __(D) to write down what went well__. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by __(E) sharing a recent win__ (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

(D)의 동사 ‘come’은 주어 ‘the beauty’와 수가 일치하지 않는 것이 명백한 어법 오류입니다. ‘the beauty’는 단수 명사이므로 동사는 ‘comes’가 되어야 합니다. ‘of integrating mini-exercises into household chores’라는 긴 수식어구 때문에 주어를 ‘chores’나 ‘exercises’로 착각하여 복수 동사를 써서는 안 됩니다. (D)가 틀린 부분입니다.

오답 (C)는 ‘what if’ 다음에 과거 시제 ‘came’이 와서 의아할 수 있지만, 이는 ‘지금 운동이 내게 다가온다면?’이라는 현실과 동떨어진 가상의 상황을 나타내는 가정법 과거입니다. 따라서 어법상 전혀 문제가 없으며, 오히려 고난도 함정 역할을 합니다.
나머지 (A), (B), (E)는 각각 동명사 주어와 단수 동사의 일치, 가주어 구문, 복수 주어와 동사의 일치가 올바르게 이루어져 있습니다. 주어와 동사 사이의 거리가 먼 구문과 가정법을 동시에 배치하여, 1등급 학생들조차 실수하기 쉬운 킬러 문항으로 설계되었습니다.
keyPoints: 주격 관계대명사절 내 동사의 수일치는 선행사에 따른다
‘what if’ + 가정법 과거는 가상의 상황을 나타내는 올바른 표현
‘the beauty’와 같은 추상명사가 주어일 때 길어진 수식어구에 현혹되지 않아야 함
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, making time for exercise __(A) is__ a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often __(B) feels__ like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout __(C) came__ to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores __(D) come__ into play. Let's be realistic; chores __(E) are__ inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They tended to call around the time (D) around which / when the trains used to run past their apartments.

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: yet we (A) hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: as long as the noise (B) didn't change you paid it no attention.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: people called the police in the middle of the night (C) claiming that something woke them up.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: the time the trains (E) used to run past their apartments.

wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 과거완료 시제는 대과거(더 먼 과거)를 나타낼 때 사용됩니다. 이 문장은 과거 어느 시점에 소음이 멈추었다는 사실을 서술하고 있으며, 그 소음이 진행되는 동안(즉, 소음이 멈춘 시점보다 더 이전부터) 우리가 그것을 알아차리지 못했음을 나타내므로 'hadn't noticed'가 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 시간을 나타내는 접속사 'as long as(…하는 동안에는)'가 이끄는 부사절 안에서, 주절의 시제(과거)와 호응하여 소음이 변하지 않는 상태를 묘사하는 것이므로 과거 시제 'didn't change'를 쓰는 것이 문법적으로 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'call the police'라는 행위와 동시에 발생하는 부대 상황(…라고 주장하면서)을 나타내기 위한 현재분사 구문입니다. 주어(people)와의 능동 관계를 올바르게 표현하여 문법적으로 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 조동사 'used to'는 과거의 규칙적인 습관이나 지속된 상태를 나타내며, 여기서는 '과거에 열차가 운행하곤 했던' 맥락을 전달합니다. 뒤에 동사 원형 'run'을 취하고 있어 어법에 맞습니다.

question.explanation: 밑줄 (D)의 'around which'는 전치사와 관계대명사의 연속으로, 앞에 선행사인 시간 명사구('the time')를 수식하는 관계절을 이끌고 있지만, 문맥상 '그들이 전화했던 바로 그 시간 즈음에'라는 의미의 시간 부사절이 와야 합니다. 따라서 관계부사 'when'을 쓰는 것이 올바릅니다. (A) 'hadn't noticed': 과거완료 시제가 '과거의 한 시점(소음이 멈춘 때)보다 더 이전의 경험(그 소리가 지속되는 동안 알아차리지 못함)'을 나타내므로 문맥상 적절합니다. (B) 'didn't change': 시간 부사절(as long as) 내에서 과거의 반복적/일반적 상황을 언급하므로 과거 시제가 적절합니다. (C) 'claiming': '사람들이 전화해서 ~라고 주장했다'라는 동시 동작 또는 부대 상황을 나타내는 분사구문으로 적절하게 사용되었습니다. (E) 'used to run': '과거에 운행하곤 했다'라는 의미로, 현재는 운행하지 않는 과거의 습관/상태를 나타내는 표현이므로 어법상 옳습니다.
keyPoints: 관계대명사 which 앞에는 선행사가 사물(시간 포함 가능)이 와야 하지만, 전치사와 함께 쓰인 'around which'는 장소나 상황을 수식하는 경향이 강하며, 명시적 시간 선행사('the time')와는 관계부사 'when'이 자연스럽게 결합합니다.
목적격 관계대명사 which가 아닌 관계부사 when을 요구하는 자리임을 파악하는 것이 핵심입니다.
question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we __(A) hadn't noticed__ the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise __(B) didn't change__ you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night __(C) claiming__ that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains __(E) used to run__ past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'that determines'는 선행사 'factor'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사절로, 문장에서 적절하게 사용되었다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'strolling'은 'found'의 목적격 보어로, 주어 'They'가 능동적으로 스스로 움직이는 상황이므로 현재분사 형태가 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 'which'는 단수 명사 'the leopard seal'을 선행사로 하며, 관계절 내 동사 'likes'는 이에 수일치되어 있고 비제한적 용법으로 적절하다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 'One penguin's destiny'는 단수 주어이므로 동사 'alters'는 수의 일치가 올바르다.

question.explanation: (D)에서 'The moment that occurs'는 시간을 나타내는 부사절로, 그 뒤에는 주절이 와야 합니다. 주절의 주어는 'the rest of the penguins'인데, 그 뒤에 현재분사 'watching'만 있을 뿐 정동사가 없으므로 비문입니다. 따라서 'watching'을 정동사 'watch'로 고쳐야 합니다. 학생들은 'watching'을 분사구문으로 보아 옳은 표현이라고 착각할 수 있지만, 이 문장은 콤마 뒤에 주절의 서술어가 반드시 필요한 구조이므로 주의해야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 분사구문과 주절 서술어 - 부사절 뒤에 주절이 올 때 '주어 + ~ing'만 있으면 동사가 누락되어 비문이 된다.
(B) 현재분사와 과거분사 - 'found strolling'에서 주어가 능동적으로 이동하므로 현재분사가 적절하다.
(E) 주어-동사 수일치 - 'One penguin's destiny'는 단수 주어이므로 단수 동사 'alters'가 맞다.
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor __(A) that determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) strolling__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(C) which likes__ to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins __(D) watching__ with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly __(A) take notice of__ the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance __(B) we've created__. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, __(C) like a car__. In our relationships, we __(D) have__ to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal __(E) not to let yourself fall out of touch__ in the first place. passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
